This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
K.S.Mudagal J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Heard.

2. Respondent No.2 in LAC No.17/2017 on the file of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and CJM at Shivamogga has preferred this appeal questioning the judgment and order passed by the said Court in rejecting her claim for disbursement of compensation for the land bearing Sy.No.107, measuring 2 acres 33 guntas of Sidlipura Village, Shivamogga District which was acquired by respondent No.1 herein for developing Industrial Area.
NC: 2024:KHC:10598-DB 3.

entities.text: I Additional Senior Civil Judge and CJM at Shivamogga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Respondent No.2/Sri. Ramesh Naik has purchased the said land under the registered sale deed dated 29.05.2006 from the appellant for consideration of Rs.72,500/-.
He made a claim before the Special Land Acquisition Officer i.e., respondent No.1 and entered into an agreement with respondent No.1, therefore a consent award was passed on 23.08.2010 in LAQ.

Sl.No.234/2009,
SPQ No.10, awarding compensation of Rs.14,00,000/- per acre.
4. Before respondent No.1, the appellant and respondent No.3 herein also made claim for the property.
Therefore, respondent No.1 referred the matter to the Civil Court exercising powers under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The Reference Court registered the same in LAC No.17/2017.

Before the Reference Court, the present respondent No.2 was respondent No.1,
appellant was respondent No.2, respondent No.3 NC: 2024:KHC:10598-DB was respondent No.3 and the present respondent No.1 was shown as the claimant.

The parties are referred to henceforth Smt Vimala vs Spl Land Acquistion Officer on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68628436/
2 as per their ranks before the Reference Court.

entities.text: Smt Vimala vs Spl Land Acquistion Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Respondent No.1 claims that he purchased the property from respondent No.2 under the registered sale deed dated 29.05.2006.
Therefore, he is the title holder to the property and entitled to claim the compensation amount.
Whereas, respondent No.2/Smt. Vimala claims that she is the absolute owner of the property.
Though she admitted the execution of registered sale deed dated 29.05.2006, she claimed that the same was not valid and legal.

She further claimed that regarding Sy.No.108 a contiguous land owned by respondent No.3, similar claim was set up by respondent No.2 and she has questioned the said sale deed in OS No.428/2012 on the file of III Addlitional Civil Judge and JMFC, Shivamogga.
NC: 2024:KHC:10598-DB

entities.text: III Addlitional Civil Judge and JMFC, Shivamogga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Therefore, she claims that she is entitled to the compensation.
Respondent No.3/Sri. Chandra Naik denied the title of respondent No.1.

He claims that he is the owner of Sy.No.108 and respondent No.2/Vimala is erstwhile owner of Sy.No.107 and they alone are entitled to receive the compensation.
6.
Before the Reference Court, on behalf of respondent No.2/Vimala, on the basis of Ex.R1 the General Power of Attorney executed by her, her husband Sri. Rudra Naik was examined as RW-1.
On their behalf, Exs.R1 to R9 were marked.
Respondents No.1 and 3 did not enter the witness box.

However, on behalf of respondent No.1, Exs.R1-1 to R1-26 were marked by way of confrontation in the cross-examination of RW-1.
7.

The Reference Court on hearing the parties, by the impugned judgment and order, rejected the claim of respondents No.2 and 3 and declared that respondent No.1/Ramesh Naik is NC:
2024:KHC:10598-DB entitled to receive the compensation of Rs.39,55,000/- in respect of land bearing Sy.No.107 measuring 2 acres 33 guntas.

The Reference Court held that respondents No.2 and 3 both admit the execution of sale deed as per Ex.R1-1 and they have failed to prove that the said sale deed was secured by playing fraud as alleged by them.
The Reference Court further held that to establish such claim, respondent No.2/Vimala should have entered the witness box, etc.
The Reference Court also took into consideration the admissions of RW-1 regarding the execution of the sale deed.

8. Dr. Revanna Bellary, learned counsel for the appellant (respondent No.2 before the Reference Court) reiterating the grounds of appeal submits that, though Vimala herself alone was the owner of Sy.No.107, the signatures of herself and Chandra Naik was taken to the sale deed relating to Sy.Nos.107 as well as 108 and the said documents NC: 2024:KHC:10598-DB are fraudulent ones.
He further submits that though the sale deed was executed, revenue records continued in the name of Vimala only, that goes to show that the sale deeds were not acted upon.
It is further contended that, Chandra Naik filed OS No.428/2012 challenging the said sale deed regarding Sy.No.108 and the Court in that suit has set aside the said sale deeds.
The Reference Court was not justified in overlooking the said judgment.
He seeks reversal of the judgment of the Reference Court.
In support of his arguments, he relied on the judgment in Meghmala and Others Vs. G. Narasimha Reddy and Others1.

entities.text: Meghmala and Others Vs. G. Narasimha Reddy and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:

3 9.

entities.text: Smt Vimala vs Spl Land Acquistion Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, Sri. R. Gopal, learned counsel for Ramesh Naik (respondent No.1 before the Reference Court) submits that, the judgment and decree in OS No.428/2012 is challenged in RA No.74/2021 before the Senior Civil Judge, (2010) 8 SCC 383 NC: 2024:KHC:10598-DB Shivamogga and interim stay is granted to the same.

He further submits that though respondent No.2/Vimala claims that the sale deed as per Ex.R1-1 was obtained by fraud, she did not plead the particulars of the fraud nor entered the witness box to substantiate the same and to face the test of cross-examination.
She has not questioned said sale deeds for all these years.
Revenue entries are not the records of the title.
She did not even make a claim before the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
He submits that considering all these aspects, the Reference Court has rightly rejected the claim of rival claimants/respondent Nos.2 and 3 and the said order does not call for interference.

10. In support of his submission, he has relied on the following judgments:
i) Prem Singh and Others Vs. Birbal and Others2, (2006) 5 SCC 353 NC:
2024:KHC:10598-DB ii) Vishwanath Bapurao Sabale Vs. Shalinibai Nagappa Sabale and Others3,
iii) Jamila Begum (Dead) through Legal Representatives Vs. Shami Mohd. (Dead)
through Legal Representatives and Another4.
11.

sentences.text:
On careful consideration of submissions of both sides and on examination of materials placed before the Court, the point that arises for determination is, "whether this matter deserves to be admitted for hearing?"
Analysis 12. Respondent No.2/Vimala and respondent No.3/Chandra Naik in their pleadings unequivocally admitted sale deed dated 29.05.2006 as per Ex.R1-1 executed by Vimala in favour of respondent No.1/ Ramesh Naik for a consideration of Rs.72,500/-.

RW-1 who is none else but the husband of (2009) 12 SCC 101 (2019) 2 SCC 727 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:10598-DB respondent No.2/Vimala and elder brother of respondent No.3/Chandra Naik, in his evidence, unequivocally admitted the execution of the said document.

In her pleadings,
Vimala only states that the said sale deed has not come into existence in proper and legal manner.

In written statement of respondent No.3, absolutely there was no whisper about legality and validity,
etc., of Ex.R1-1.
Even in the evidence of RW-1, nothing was elicited to establish the fraud or misrepresentation, etc., in execution of the sale deed.
13. Only for the first time in the argument, it was alleged that the sale deed was obtained by fraud.
Even before this Court also, the same contentions were urged.
Order VI Rule 4 of CPC requires that,

if any party pleads fraud, undue influence, misrepresentation, etc., he should plead the particulars of Smt Vimala vs Spl Land Acquistion Officer on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68628436/
4 the same.

entities.text: Smt Vimala vs Spl Land Acquistion Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But the same was not alleged by respondents No.2 and 3 in the present - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:10598-DB case.

Even as per the judgment in Meghmala's case referred to supra relied on by learned counsel for the appellant, para No.33 of the said judgment held that "fraud involves two elements, deceit and injury to the person deceived."
If any person claims that he is deceived or injured, that is personal to him, to establish that, he has to enter the witness box and face the test of cross-examination.
In the present case, respondent No.2/Vimala did not enter the witness box for the reasons best known to her.
Even her husband RW-1 in his deposition did not whisper anything regarding fraud, undue influence or misrepresentation.

Once the execution of the registered sale deed is admitted, the presumption under Section 114 of Indian Evidence Act, 1872 comes into play and the presumption is that the sale deed is validly executed.

Illustration (e) and (i)
of Section 114 reads thus:
"114.

The Court may presume the existence of any fact which it thinks likely to have happened, regard being had to the common course of - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:10598-DB natural events, human conduct and public and private business, in their relation to the facts of the particular case.

Illustrations:
The Court may presume -- .........
(e) that judicial and official acts have been regularly performed;
.........
(i) that when a document creating an obligation is in the hands of the obligor, the obligation has been discharged."

14. In the judgments in Prem Singh's case and Vishwanath Bapurao Sabale's case referred to supra,
the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the registered documents are presumed to be validly executed.
Therefore, the burden is on the person who claims that the same was not validly executed.
The above discussion shows that such presumption was not rebutted.
The contesting respondents did not even challenge the sale deed as per Ex.R1-1 for all these years.

It is now submitted that respondent No.2/Vimala has filed a suit in March 2024 - 13 - Smt Vimala vs Spl Land Acquistion Officer on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68628436/
5 NC: 2024:KHC:10598-DB challenging the said sale deed.

entities.text: Vimala vs Spl Land Acquistion Officer on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Firstly, nothing is placed to substantiate the said contention.
Secondly, the alleged challenge is after 18 years of the execution of the sale deed and it is not known how far the said case sustains.
15. Relying on the decree said to have been passed in OS No.428/2012 as per Ex.R2, it was contended that the sale deed is cancelled.
The said suit is related to Sy.No.108 and not about Sy.No.107.
It is not in dispute that the said judgment is challenged by respondent No.1/Ramesh Naik in RA No.74/2021 before the Senior Civil Judge, Shivamogga and the same is stayed.

Therefore, the said judgment is of no assistance to the appellant to say that the sale deed relating to Sy.No.107 was fraudulent one, etc.
16.
On examining the material on record and the aforesaid judicial precedents, it is not a fit case for admission.
- 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:10598-DB ORDER
The appeal is dismissed with costs.
